title: Who Picks First? Compensatory Fairness When Equal Division Is Impossible
abstract: arXiv:2611.09685v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: When indivisible objects, such as heirlooms or tickets to sports events, do not divide evenly among agents with equal claims, some agents must receive more objects than others. Can picking first compensate those with fewer objects? We propose two principles of compensatory fairness. An agent with fewer objects must not envy a larger bundle with any one of its objects removed, and priority advantages among agents with equally many objects must alternate rather than accumulate. Non-wastefulness, neutrality and an object-wise form of Maskin monotonicity characterize the draft rules, in which agents pick in a fixed sequence. Adding the two principles and envy-freeness up to one object singles out the block--snake draft, in which agents with fewer objects pick first in every round and each group's order reverses between rounds. Among draft rules, compensation is compatible with strategy-proofness, but envy-freeness up to one object is not: on

translated_title: 谁先挑选？当均等分配不可能实现时的补偿公平性
translated_abstract: 当不可分割的物品（如传家宝或体育赛事门票）无法在具有同等权利的代理人之间均等分配时，某些代理人必然会比其他人获得更多的物品。先挑选能否补偿那些获得物品较少的代理人？我们提出了补偿公平的两个原则：物品较少的代理人不得嫉妒移除任意一件物品后的更大物品束，且在拥有相同数量物品的代理人之间，优先权优势应当交替而非累积。非浪费性、中立性以及一种按物品形式的Maskin单调性共同刻画了“抽选规则”（即代理人按固定顺序依次挑选的规则）。在此之上加入这两项原则以及“至多嫉妒一件物品”的公平性（envy-freeness up to one object）后，可唯一确定“块-蛇形抽选”规则：在该规则中，物品较少的代理人在每一轮都先挑选，且每个组内的顺序在轮与轮之间反转。在抽选规则中，补偿与策略防操纵性是兼容的，但“至多嫉妒一件物品”的公平性则无法实现。
tldr: 本文针对不可分割物品无法均分的分配问题提出补偿公平原则，证明该原则可将公平规则刻画为抽选规则，并唯一确定“块-蛇形抽选”（物品少者每轮先选、组内顺序逐轮反转），同时表明补偿与策略防操纵性兼容但与“至多嫉妒一件物品”公平性不兼容。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes two principles of compensatory fairness for allocating indivisible objects that cannot be equally divided, characterizes draft rules and uniquely identifies the block-snake draft—where agents with fewer objects pick first each round and each group's order reverses between rounds—showing that compensation is compatible with strategy-proofness but not with envy-freeness up to one object.
